newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA MAY DELAY HIS RACE RETURN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA MAY DELAY HIS RACE RETURN.

text.p: Italian Alpine skiing champion Alberto Tomba said on Thursday he might have to wait until next year before making his return to World Cup racing.
"The most important thing is to be ready for the world championships in February," Tomba was quoted as saying in the Turin sports daily newspaper Tuttosport.
"Maybe I won't make it in time for Campiglio on December 17, maybe I'll have to leave it until Kranjska Gora on January 5 and 6. We'll have to wait and see.
"The Campiglio slalom is the shortest, so maybe I'll be there. I'll decide a week before the race."

Tomba started training again in the Alpine resort of Sestriere, which hosts the 1997 world championships, earlier this month after falling heavily in training on a glacier in October and injuring a wrist and knee.

Tomba, who won two gold medals at the world championships in Spain this year to go with his three Olympic golds, has said he hoped to return at the race in Madonna di Campiglio, two days before his 30th birthday.
The Italian was quoted as saying on Thursday, however, that his wrist still gave him considerable pain and made it difficult for him to push hard, particularly in the giant.

"Imagine what it's going to be like when I get to the starting gate of a slalom with an icy piste. We'll see, we'll see when I train on hard pistes, at the moment I don't know what to say," the newspaper quoted him as saying.
